title: Ukrainian As a Foreign Language: an online course for beginners
usedFor: English-language explanations of grammar for beginners: no articles, flexible word order and three genders (Lesson 1); gender endings as a rule of thumb with exceptions such as ніч, ім’я, Микола, and the advice to learn each noun with its gender (Lesson 4); seven cases and why word order can be flexible, with сестра as the case example (Lesson 5); aspect pairs and no present tense for perfectives (Lesson 6); the subject 'you' omitted when clear from context (Lesson 5 dialogue); six present-tense verb endings for six persons, the two conjugation groups, past-tense endings by gender and number, ви with plural forms, the two imperfective futures and the perfective simple future (Lesson 7); adjective endings -ий/-а/-е (Lesson 9); flexible word order, known information first and new information last, не fixed before the word it negates, the omitted verb 'to be' (Микола студент, 'this is…' sentences), and yes/no questions made by intonation alone (Lesson 10); ти and ви usage (Lesson 11).
notes: A free eleven-lesson course on the university's English-language site, written by a native speaker in Kyiv. Older pages in windows-1251 encoding. Its Ukrainian examples were not copied: every example on this site was rechecked in goroh-dictionary. Lesson pages are lesson1.htm to lesson11.htm under the course URL.
